# Book-aligned learning map

**Book:** Ivan Savov, *No Bullshit Guide to Linear Algebra*, second edition, version 2.2, Minireference Co. The file you uploaded is a **152-page extended preview** of the **596-page full book**. Its table of contents provides full chapter coverage, but excerpts do not contain every paragraph, exercise, proof or solution from the full book. We should not imply otherwise.

The source preview foregrounds two principles: **linearity preserves combinations**, and **a linear map on two-dimensional inputs is determined by what it does to two basis directions**. Our recurring matrix example builds from that foundation.

| Source chapter | Named subjects in the book's contents | New tutorial |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Math fundamentals | Equations, numbers, functions, algebra, trigonometry, vectors, complex numbers and systems | [Mathematical prerequisites](01-math-foundations/index.qmd) |
| 2. Intro to linear algebra | Definitions, vector operations, matrix operations, linearity | [Vectors and matrices](02-intro-linear-algebra/index.qmd) |
| 3. Computational linear algebra | RREF, equations, multiplication, determinant and inverse | [Matrix computations](03-computational-linear-algebra/index.qmd) |
| 4. Geometric aspects | Lines and planes, projections, coordinate projections, vector spaces | [Geometry](04-geometric-linear-algebra/index.qmd) |
| 5. Linear transformations | Linear maps, matrix representation, change of basis and invertibility | [Linear maps](05-linear-transformations/index.qmd) |
| 6. Theoretical linear algebra | Eigenvectors, abstract spaces, inner products, Gram–Schmidt and decompositions | [Theory](06-theoretical-linear-algebra/index.qmd) |
| 7. Applications | Chemistry, economics, circuits, graphs, least squares, graphics, codes and Fourier analysis | [Applications](07-applications/index.qmd) |
| 8. Probability theory | Distributions, Markov chains and PageRank | [Probability](08-probability/index.qmd) |
| 9. Quantum mechanics | Dirac notation, postulates, quantum information and polarisation | [Quantum mathematics](09-quantum-mechanics/index.qmd) |

The first six book chapters form the core course; Chapters 7–9 show broader applications. The book's Chapter 1 provides prerequisites for students who need them.

## A preview is not a full-text source

Where the preview includes an excerpt (for example, the introduction's tablet-to-wall demonstration), the curriculum may explain that idea in new language with different numeric transformations. Where only the full-book **table of contents** indicates coverage, the course draws on standard mathematical definitions to build a **clearly labelled independent tutorial**, not a supposed paraphrase of unseen source pages.

The reference is for **concept selection and study order**. This website does not copy full-book figures, diagrams or solved exercise answers.

## Suggested study route

If algebra and functions already feel familiar, begin at [vectors and matrices](02-intro-linear-algebra/index.qmd). Otherwise start with [equations](01-math-foundations/01-solving-equations.qmd). Learn [matrix multiplication](03-computational-linear-algebra/03-matrix-multiplication.qmd) before [linear transformations](05-linear-transformations/01-what-linearity-means.qmd), and [basis](04-geometric-linear-algebra/03-basis-and-dimension.qmd) before [eigenvectors](06-theoretical-linear-algebra/01-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.qmd).

## How every equation should be explained

A formula is only the compact end of a thought. For each one we must define **all** symbols, demonstrate a concrete substitution, explain the relevant invariant or theorem, and state when assumptions fail.
